title: Tech Mahindra Profit Jumps 28% as Deal Wins Cross $1 Billion for Third Straight Quarter
excerpt: India's fifth-largest IT firm posted ₹1,465 crore in net profit and $1.08 billion in new deal bookings for Q1 FY27, beating revenue estimates on broad-based growth.
body:
• Tech Mahindra's Q1 FY27 net profit rose 28.4% year-on-year to ₹1,465 crore, while revenue climbed 17.7% to ₹15,712 crore, beating analyst estimates.
  • New deal wins totaled $1.08 billion in total contract value, marking the third consecutive quarter above the $1 billion mark and a 33.3% YoY increase.
  • EBIT margin expanded 70 basis points sequentially to 14.4%, reflecting continued operational improvement under CEO Mohit Joshi's turnaround plan.
  • Headcount declined by 863 to 146,760, while the company's $50 million-plus client base grew by seven accounts.

Tech Mahindra reported a strong first quarter for fiscal 2027, with consolidated net profit rising 28.4% year-on-year to ₹1,465 crore for the three months ended June 30, 2026. Revenue from operations grew 17.7% to ₹15,712 crore, comfortably ahead of analyst expectations of ₹15,476 crore compiled by LSEG.

The results mark a continued acceleration in the Pune-headquartered company's turnaround, with all business verticals posting year-on-year growth and deal momentum remaining elevated. Shares rose about 3% in the session following the earnings release.

Revenue Beat Driven by Manufacturing and Communications

Revenue growth was powered by the company's communications and manufacturing segments, according to Reuters, alongside a weaker rupee that boosted the value of overseas earnings. In constant currency terms, revenue came in at $1,660 million, up 6.6% annually and 2.6% sequentially.

Geographically, Europe was the standout performer, growing 8.1% quarter-on-quarter and 12.1% year-on-year to contribute 27.5% of total revenue. The Americas, at 48.6% of the mix, grew 4.8% on an annual basis, while the rest of the world accounted for 23.9%.

"YoY growth of 6.1% coupled with three consecutive quarters of deal wins exceeding $1 billion underscores the resilience of our business and the growing relevance of our offerings."

— Mohit Joshi, CEO and Managing Director, Tech Mahindra

Deal Pipeline Hits New Highs

New deal bookings reached a total contract value of $1,078 million, up 33.3% from $809 million in the year-ago quarter. This was the third straight quarter in which deal wins exceeded the $1 billion threshold — a milestone that underscores growing enterprise demand for Tech Mahindra's offerings in AI, cloud, and digital transformation.

The company's $50 million-plus client base expanded by seven accounts on a year-on-year basis, signaling deeper penetration into large enterprise relationships.

Margin Expansion Continues

Operating EBIT rose 9.2% sequentially to ₹2,264 crore, pushing the EBIT margin up 70 basis points to 14.4% from 13.7% in the March quarter. Free cash flow for the period stood at $167 million.

Earnings per share expanded to ₹16.53 from ₹12.87 a year earlier. Cash and equivalents at quarter-end stood at ₹9,695 crore.

While revenue comfortably beat consensus, net profit came in slightly below analyst expectations of roughly ₹1,694 crore, reflecting some cost pressures during the quarter.

"We remain committed to building a future-ready organisation through continued investments in differentiated capabilities, domain-specific and sovereign AI, platforms, and talent."

— Rohit Anand, Chief Financial Officer, Tech Mahindra

Headcount and Attrition

Total headcount at the end of Q1 stood at 146,760, a sequential decline of 863 employees. Last-twelve-month IT attrition was 11.8%, in line with the broader industry trend of cautious hiring amid ongoing automation and efficiency drives across Indian IT services firms.

What's Next for Tech Mahindra

Analysts noted that Tech Mahindra was on track to post the strongest growth among large Indian IT services firms in Q1 FY27, according to Reuters. The sustained deal momentum and margin trajectory lend credibility to CEO Mohit Joshi's multi-quarter turnaround blueprint.

For investors in the Indian diaspora tracking IT sector performance, the results reinforce a broader pattern: India's major IT exporters are navigating macro uncertainty through AI-driven service offerings and operational discipline, with Tech Mahindra emerging as one of the faster growers in the peer group.
